finding.claim: Webhook callback URLs are stored with no validation and later POSTed to by the server, so any caller of /subscribe can make the server send requests to internal hosts. That includes cloud metadata, loopback and private ranges. The payload is controlled by the server, but the attacker chooses the destination, scheme and port. The request is sent every minute, and the response is discarded, so this is blind SSRF.
finding.source: callbackUrl body parameter of POST /subscribe (Jobs.subscribe, line 13)

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-supplied URL
URL is stored unvalidated in the static subscriptions map
notifyAll iterates subscriptions.values() on the minute schedule
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI with no scheme, host or IP check
client.send issues the POST to the attacker-chosen destination

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, resolved-IP check, or DNS pinning exists anywhere on the path. No authentication is visible in this file. HttpClient.newHttpClient() does not follow redirects by default, which only removes the redirect-based variant. The response is not returned to the caller, so impact is limited to blind SSRF: internal POST requests and port or host probing through timing or errors. Most other cloud metadata services (for example IMDSv1 and GCP) need GET or special headers, so the metadata impact is limited.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and :21/:24 pass it to URI.create and client.send with no scheme, host or IP check, and the only regex guard (:30) is on the unrelated thumb() path. No authentication or other validation exists anywhere in the codebase, so this is blind SSRF.
